title: Bur Oak: Ancient Prairie Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: Four of these five were standing before Chicago was. Bur oaks mapped in Chicago and Washington DC, the oldest estimated at 375 years.
intro: Four of these five were standing before Chicago was. The bur oak is the prairie oak, its bark thick enough to survive the grass fires that once kept the Midwest open, so the old ones left in the city are survivors of the savanna it was built across. One in the grove on Wooded Island blew down around 2016 and its rings were counted back to roughly 1730. The oldest in the Union Ridge Cemetery savanna is put at 325 to 375 years. The oak on the Midway Plaisance was left standing when everything around it was cleared and regraded for the 1893 World's Fair. Local history makes a fourth a witness tree the Potawatomi used to find the route back to the Des Plaines River. Washington's is the exception: Frederick Law Olmsted Jr. kept it in the 1930s while clearing about 250 trees out of Union Square.
